title: Do you think devs will ever update MZ to use pixiJS v8?

posts.author: Codesterz33
posts.body:
I'm not a tech expert and coding knowledge is pretty limited. A long standing issue I've had with RPG Maker is poor/uneven performance. I have a dated but decent enough PC. Ryzen 3700x, 32 gb ram, RTX 2700 super. Despite this pretty much ALL rpg maker MV/MZ/Ace/VX Ace games has these random poor performance moments. It's not an FPS drop its more like a stutter or jitter. RPG maker still says the game is running at 60fps even though something is clearly going wrong. It's weird because I'll be on a map and the game is running fine, then go to another map and return to the same map and despite nothing having changed the performance has degraded. Going back and forth between maps will randomly fix it. Sometimes switching alt tabbing to something else then returning will cause it to happen as well.
I don't know if Pixi is the issue here or something else maybe another case of javascript being bad for games. What I have been seeing though is Pixi has recently received a big update that boasts much better performance. I can't help but wonder if RPG Maker MZ will ever see this integrated into it with an update. Do you think this will ever happen or maybe a community project if possible? I have messed around with the idea of making an RPG maker game before, but I just can't get behind the idea of using it when there is something clearly wrong internally with it.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
peq42_ said:
They kinda abandoned MV,
Click to expand...
I hope this is poor word choice.
They didn't "abandon" MV. MV was upgraded to MZ, deprecating MV as legacy software.
MZ is the current and actively supported version of the software. You cannot expect every company to continue to support legacy software for free.
Nevertheless, the OP is referring to MZ, not MV anyways.
I don't really have time to go into my usual technical spiel about how the engine works and utilizes your hardware, but to address the topic title;
unlikely.
iirc, the newer versions of PIXI made some radical changes that would likely break large parts of RM's renderer, as well as hamper plugins.
It would: A) just be a bad business decision to - this late in MZ's life cycle - to push an update that would brick half of the community made support for the software. B ) likely cause problems within the engine itself, which would cost more development time to fix when I think GGG is in a position looking to recoup costs.
Finally, upgrading PIXI
~might~
improve visual performance and frame times, but by how much is not really known. It may only be a marginal performance increase - imperceptible by your average user.
Likely your problems come down to:
How your system is utilizing resources (such as background tasks)
How the game you play/make are being developed and optimized
Or other system related errors, such as throttled performance caused by read/write speeds or overheating.

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
I doubt they will. They tried to update pixi with a version of MZ and the result was some users couldn't run the engine anymore, or test play froze, or both. So they had to roll it back as a result.
And as stated it would brick most plugins which would not go over well at all.
However, if hitting performance issues playing games, check these things:
ACE: Ace uses rgssx which the player for it can get weird on windows10 I found. Sometimes a system restart fixes that (and I mean a literal restart, as in select restart in windows. Do not just turn it off and on again, win10 changes how that works).
MV/MZ: Make sure the games are using  your graphics card, not the built in one. The engine loves to default to the built in one which often causes issues.

posts.author: Radibor78
posts.body:
I recently tinkered a bit with the core code of RPG Maker MZ and also had a look at how to update the NWJS and PIXI version.
RPG Maker MZ
For those who are interested, I have built packages for the different core versions with instructions on how to exchange these components and added the code of a correspondingly adapted core. The whole thing uses NWJS v0.94.0 and PIXI v7.4.2 - i.e. the latest NWJS version and the latest v7 of PIXI. The changes to the Maker Core are quite straightforward and rather minimal. This means that plugins should continue to work (as long as they don't talk directly to PIXI or overwrite the initialize functions of some base classes in the core without calling the original version, which should hardly be the case).
The versions can be downloaded from my website at
https://radibor78lp.de/downloads/
. I will also post updates of the packages there if there are any adjustments to be made. The whole thing can be used freely by anyone in games, but it is a work-in-progress and has not yet been intensively tested, so that certain functions may still require adjustments.
RPG Maker MV
For RPG Maker MV there is also a package that contains a description of how to update to NWJS v0.94.0 and PIXI v4.8.9 (the last v4 version). Here you can also replace the standard 32bit version of NWJS with the 64bit version, so that the game can also run as a 64bit process in the test and/or deployment state. If you want to keep the NWJS version, you can also use the description for replacing NWJS to simply download and install the 64bit version of the current version used by the Maker. The core file included in the MV package is not strictly necessary. There are only a few lines changed to get rid of some warning messages after the PIXI update.
In any case, only a few simple steps are required to exchange the versions and can be easily reverted in case of problems.
